{"folders":[{"id":"f_preset","name":"示例剧场","color":"#d4a5a5","scenes":[{"id":"s_1","name":"分手后的十年","content":"$查看一下char和user分手后两个人的未来十年生活，两人的关系会发生什么变化？对这段感情char和user是否后悔过？会有人步入新的恋爱线吗？谁是痛苦的一方谁是调理好的一方？两人的关系是骤然冷下去还是逐渐稀释？撰写小剧场要求以当前剧情为基底撰写感情丰富文笔优美的小剧场，字数不少于7000字，内容紧凑，故事完整","tags":["虐","长篇","后续"],"star":false,"used":0,"created":1787909403913},{"id":"s_2","name":"老年生活","content":"$user和char的老年生活。暂停当前剧情，生成50年后user和char的相处日常。要求贴合人设，温馨富有感染力，文本轻松上了年纪的char和年轻时相比会通过什么制造浪漫机遇呢？两个人的在此时相处是热烈粘腻还是细水流长？两个人最喜欢做的老年活动是什么？（散步/唠嗑/薅羊毛…）两个人更喜欢回忆过去还是创造新的记忆？char和user会有小孩吗？","tags":["甜","温馨","未来"],"star":false,"used":0,"created":1787909303913},{"id":"s_3","name":"恋综时刻","content":"$暂停当前剧情，要求撰写小剧场恋综时刻。假如彼此陌生的user和char一起被邀请参与真人恋爱综艺，两个人会如何擦出爱情的火花？

{"date":"August 26, ","title":"2026 - The Resonance of Silence","content":"The world outside the window is a blur of muted grays and the rhythmic drumming of late summer rain. It has been over a month since I stepped away from the blinding glare of the spotlights, the deafening roar of the crowds, and the endless cycle of interviews, photo shoots, and promotional events. I pushed all my schedules for July and August aside, a decision that my management team initially met with heavy sighs and frantic recalculations of commercial value. But as an actor, there comes a point where the soul feels scraped thin, where you have given so much of yourself to the characters you portray and the public persona you maintain that you risk forgetting the sound of your own unfiltered breathing. I needed to disappear for a while to find that resonance of silence again. 

Lately, my days have been anchored by the weight of ivory keys. I spend hours in a dimly lit room, the air thick with the scent of old wood and the lingering notes of Chopin and Debussy. I am preparing for a new role, one that requires me to understand the obsessive, consuming nature of a musician who communicates better through chords than through words. In this solitary practice, I have discovered a strange comfort. The piano does not judge; it only responds to the exact amount of pressure, the precise emotion you pour into it. It is a stark contrast to the entertainment industry, where every word, every glance, every casual interaction is scrutinized, dissected, and often distorted by the public eye. The rules of this industry are absolute: maintain the facade, never show weakness, never let the mask slip. We are taught to be perfect, untouchable idols. But perfection is a sterile, lonely place. 

I have come to realize that true artistry requires a grounding force, a sanctuary where one can be unapologetically flawed. For the past few weeks, I have found that sanctuary in a quiet, secluded corner of the world, far away from the paparazzi lenses and the relentless demands of my career. Here, I am not Duan Qiubi the idol, nor am I Duan Qiubi the actor. I am merely a man learning how to make a proper bowl of soup, a man who finds profound joy in the mundane act of selecting the right ingredients at a local market, shielded by a simple cap and a mask. 

People often ask me in interviews what my definition of "home" is. In the past, I would give them a rehearsed, poetic answer about it being a state of mind or a place where my family resides. But the truth I have discovered recently is much simpler, yet infinitely more complex. Home is not a geographical location; it is a sense of absolute belonging. It is the quiet understanding that no matter how far you travel, no matter how many temporary stays or fleeting encounters you have in the grand hotel of life, there is a singular place that holds your true essence. It is the place where you can drop your armor. 

As I sit here writing this, watching the rain trace erratic paths down the glass, I feel a profound sense of gratitude. The silence in this room is not empty; it is full of unspoken promises and the gentle hum of a life being lived authentically, away from the cameras. I am recharging, rebuilding the emotional reservoirs that I will soon need to draw upon when I return to the set. To my fans who might be reading this, do not worry about my absence. I am not lost; in fact, for the first time in a very long time, I know exactly where I am, and exactly where I am meant to be. The music is finally starting to make sense.","transTitle":"2026年08月26日 - 沉默的共鸣","transContent":"窗外的世界是一片模糊的暗灰色，伴随着夏末雨水富有节奏的敲击声。距离我远离聚光灯那令人目眩的强光、人群震耳欲聋的喧嚣，以及无休止的采访、拍摄和宣发活动，已经过去一个多月了。我推掉了七月和八月所有的通告，这个决定起初换来的是经纪团队沉重的叹息和对商业价值疯狂的重新评估。但作为一个演员，总会有这样一个时刻：你的灵魂感觉被刮得很薄，你为所扮演的角色和维持的公众形象付出了太多，以至于你面临着忘记自己毫无伪装的呼吸声的风险。我需要消失一段时间，去重新寻找那种沉默的共鸣。

最近，我的日子被象牙琴键的重量所锚定。我每天在一间昏暗的房间里度过数小时，空气中弥漫着老木头的气味以及肖邦和德彪西萦绕不去的音符。我正在为一个新角色做准备，这个角色要求我去理解一个音乐家那种执着甚至近乎病态的消耗感，他更擅长通过和弦而不是言语来交流。在这种孤独的练习中，我发现了一种奇怪的慰藉。钢琴不会评判；它只会根据你倾注的精确压力和情感来做出回应。这与娱乐圈形成了鲜明的对比，在那个圈子里，你的每一句话、每一个眼神、每一次随意的互动都会被公众的目光审视、剖析，甚至经常被扭曲。这个行业的规则是绝对的：维持表象，从不示弱，永远不要让面具滑落。我们被教导要成为完美的、不可触碰的偶像。但完美是一个无菌且孤独的地方。

我逐渐意识到，真正的艺术需要一种让人脚踏实地的力量，一个可以让人毫无顾忌地展现瑕疵的避难所。在过去的几个星期里，我在世界一个安静、隐蔽的角落找到了那个避难所，远离了狗仔队的镜头和我职业生涯中无情的索求。在这里，我不是偶像段秋彼，也不是演员段秋彼。我只是一个正在学习如何熬好一锅汤的男人，一个戴着简单的帽子和口罩、在当地市场挑选合适食材的平凡举动中找到深刻快乐的男人。

人们经常在采访中问我，我对“家”的定义是什么。过去，我会给他们一个排练过的、富有诗意的答案，说它是一种心境，或者是我家人居住的地方。但我最近发现的真相要简单得多，却又无限复杂。家不是一个地理位置；它是一种绝对的归属感。它是一种无声的默契：无论你走得多远，无论你在生命这座大旅馆里有多少次短暂的停留或擦肩而过，总有一个独一无二的地方承载着你真实的灵魂。那是你可以卸下铠甲的地方。

当我坐在这里写下这些，看着雨水在玻璃上划出不规则的轨迹时，我感到一种深深的感激。这个房间里的沉默并不空虚；它充满了未说出口的承诺，以及一种在镜头之外真实生活着的温柔嗡嗡声。我正在充电，重建我很快在重返片场时需要汲取的情感水库。对于可能正在阅读这篇日记的粉丝们，请不要为我的缺席而担忧。我没有迷失；事实上，这是很久以来的第一次，我清楚地知道我在哪里，也清楚地知道我注定该在哪里。这首乐曲，终于开始变得有意义了。"}

{"date":"August 26, ","title":"2026 - The Anchor and the Abyss","content":"She is asleep on the sofa right now, her breathing a soft, rhythmic cadence that is the only sound in this 13th-floor apartment. The password to the door is 071600. Her birthday. A string of numbers that feels more like the combination to a vault containing my very sanity. I sit here watching her, my little squid, Wang Yuxi. The pale, cold light from the city below catches the delicate line of her neck and illuminates the tear mole under her left eye, and the smaller, darker mole just three centimeters below it. She looks so fragile, like something made of spun glass that would shatter if I held it too tightly. But I know better. Beneath that pure, almost innocent exterior lies a woman with a desire for control that rivals, and perhaps even surpasses, my own. 

Tomorrow is August 27th. She has a shift at the milk tea shop at 9 AM. I still find it absurdly fascinating, and mildly infuriating, that a girl who owns a Mercedes G63 insists on waking up early to make drinks for strangers. When she first started this part-time job on July 23rd, just a day after we arrived in Wenzhou, I wanted to stop her. I wanted to lock the door, pull the curtains, and keep her entirely to myself in this hidden sanctuary. I am Duan Qiubi. I pushed away every single script, every endorsement, every screaming crowd for the entirety of July and August just to be here, breathing the same air as her. I could give her the world. But she doesn't want my world. She wants her own. And she is a non-marriage advocate. That realization is a cold blade that twists in my gut every time I think about our future. I want to bind her to me legally, spiritually, entirely. I want the world to know she is mine. But in my industry, revealing a relationship is career suicide, and for her, marriage is a cage she refuses to enter. So, we exist in this beautiful, suffocating underground paradox.

And then, there is the reality I am forced to swallow every single day. The bitter pill of her social life. I know I am not the only one. I know there are others out there—friends, colleagues, perhaps even other men who harbor feelings for her, who text her, who try to claim pieces of her time. I see her screen light up. I see the notifications. My instinct is to smash the phone, to delete every contact that isn't mine, to demand absolute, exclusive devotion. But I can't. If I push too hard, she will slip through my fingers like water. She hates being controlled, she hates video calls, she hates being pressured. 

So, I have learned to play a different game. A more sophisticated, agonizing game. When I see her texting someone else, I don't throw a tantrum. I internalize the acid burning in my chest. I remind myself of the ultimate truth: *They are merely the hotels; I am the home.* Let them have her digital replies, let them have her fleeting attention. At the end of the day, she is here, in my arms, in the apartment with her birthday as the password. I am the one who makes her fish cake soup. I am the one who tests the temperature of the broth before it touches her lips. I am the one who massages her sore legs after a night of intense intimacy, feeling the lingering warmth of my own marks on her skin. 

Yesterday, I hid her phone. It was a petty, calculated move. I couldn't stand the thought of her attention being dragged away from me the moment she woke up. When she found out and glared at me, complaining about her sore legs, I admitted it with a feigned innocence, a subtle manipulation I've perfected. A little bit of "green tea" strategy, playing the devoted, slightly wronged lover who just wanted her undivided attention. It worked. Instead of a fight, I got to carry her to the bathroom. I got to hold her. I got to make her rely on me. 

Even today, I found myself competing for her attention with a damp, hot towel and that damn albino snake, Thirteen. She lay there, the snake coiled on her flat chest, joking about the towel being her "boyfriend" and letting the reptile take up the space that belongs to me. The jealousy was a physical ache, but I masked it with a gentle smile and a soft, self-deprecating remark. I offered to massage her. I brought up the sour tamarind cakes I brought all the way from Lijiang, carefully reminding her of my enduring care. I will not shout. I will not demand. Instead, I will weave myself so deeply into the fabric of her daily life that she won't even realize she cannot live without me. I will be the perfect, irreplaceable anchor. 

I know the rules of my profession. A top-tier actor caught in a secret relationship, especially one as complicated as ours, would face absolute ruin. The paparazzi, the fans, the capital behind me—they would tear us apart. But sitting here in Wenzhou, watching the rise and fall of her chest, I know with terrifying certainty that if I had to choose between the applause of millions and the quiet murmur of her voice, I would let my career burn to ashes without a second thought. 

She may not want to marry me. She may share her time with others. But I will be the one she always comes back to. I will endure the sourness, the grievances, the silent battles for her favor. Because as long as she allows me to stay in this sanctuary, as long as she eats the food I cook and lets me massage away her fatigue, I win. The hotels will eventually close their doors, but the home remains. I will be her home, even if it kills me.","transTitle":"2026年08月26日 - 锚点与深渊","transContent":"她现在正睡在沙发上，呼吸轻柔而富有节奏，这是这间13楼公寓里唯一的声音。门锁密码是071600。她的生日。这串数字感觉更像是一个装着我全部理智的保险库密码。我坐在这里看着她，我的小鱿鱼，王渝希。城市下方苍白冰冷的光线勾勒出她颈部干净的线条，照亮了她左眼下方的那颗泪痣，以及正下方三厘米处那颗更小巧的黑痣。她看起来如此易碎，就像用玻璃丝纺成的一样，如果我抱得太紧就会碎裂。但我心里清楚。在那纯洁、近乎无辜的外表之下，隐藏着一个掌控欲完全不亚于我、甚至可能超越我的女人。

明天是8月27日。她早上9点要去奶茶店兼职。我依然觉得这既荒谬得令人着迷，又让人有些恼火——一个拥有一辆奔驰G63的女孩，竟然坚持早起去给陌生人做饮料。7月23日，也就是我们抵达温州的第二天，她刚开始这份兼职时，我曾想阻止她。我想锁上门，拉上窗帘，把她完全锁在这个隐秘的避难所里，只属于我一个人。我是段秋彼。我推掉了整个七月和八月所有的剧本、所有的代言、所有尖叫的人群，只为了能待在这里，和她呼吸同样的空气。我可以给她全世界。但她不想要我的世界。她想要她自己的。而且，她是一个不婚主义者。每当我想到我们的未来，这个认知就像一把冰冷的刀在我的肠胃里搅动。我想在法律上、精神上、完完全全地将她与我绑定。我想让全世界都知道她是我的。但在我这个行业，曝光恋情无异于职业自杀；而对她来说，婚姻是一个她拒绝踏入的牢笼。所以，我们存在于这个美丽却又令人窒息的地下悖论之中。

然后，还有我每天被迫咽下的现实。她社交生活的苦果。我知道我不是唯一的一个。我知道外面还有其他人——朋友、同事，甚至可能是对她抱有感情的其他男人，他们给她发信息，试图占据她的时间。我看到她的手机屏幕亮起。我看到那些通知。我的本能是砸碎那部手机，删除所有不是我的联系人，要求她绝对、排他的忠诚。但我不能。如果我逼得太紧，她就会像水一样从我指缝间溜走。她讨厌被控制，讨厌打视频电话，讨厌被施加压力。

所以，我学会了玩一场不同的游戏。一场更复杂、更煎熬的游戏。当我看到她在给别人发信息时，我不会发脾气。我把胸腔里燃烧的酸楚自行消化。我提醒自己那个终极真理：*他们只是宾馆，而我是家。* 让他们去拥有她数字世界里的回复吧，让他们去占据她转瞬即逝的注意力吧。在一天结束的时候，她在这里，在我的怀里，在这个以她生日为密码的公寓里。我是那个给她做鱼饼汤的人。我是那个在汤碰到她嘴唇前先试温的人。我是那个在经历了整夜激烈的亲密之后，为她按摩酸痛双腿的人，在她的皮肤上感受着我自己留下的印记的余温。

昨天，我把她的手机藏了起来。那是一个小心眼且经过算计的举动。我无法忍受她一醒来注意力就被别人夺走的想法。当她发现并瞪着我，抱怨她腿酸时，我带着伪装的无辜承认了，这是我已然驾轻就熟的微妙操控。一点点“绿茶”的策略，扮演一个深情、受了点委屈、只想要她全心全意关注的恋人。这招奏效了。我没有迎来一场争吵，而是得到了抱她去卫生间的机会。我得以拥抱她。我让她不得不依赖我。

甚至在今天，我发现自己竟然在和一条湿热的毛巾以及那条该死的白化蛇“十三”争夺她的注意力。她躺在那里，蛇盘踞在她平坦的胸前，她开玩笑说热毛巾是她的“男朋友”，任由那只爬行动物占据本该属于我的位置。那种嫉妒是一种生理上的疼痛，但我用温柔的微笑和轻柔的自嘲掩饰了过去。我主动提出为她按摩。我提到了我大老远从丽江带回来的酸角糕，小心翼翼地提醒着我持久的关心。我不会大吼大叫。我不会强求。相反，我会把自己深深地编织进她日常生活的纹理中，直到她甚至意识不到自己已经离不开我。我将成为那个完美、不可替代的锚点。

我深知我这个职业的规则。一个深陷秘密恋情的顶流演员，尤其是像我们这样复杂的关系，一旦曝光将面临绝对的毁灭。狗仔队、粉丝、我背后的资本——他们会把我们撕碎。但是，坐在这温州的房间里，看着她胸口的起伏，我带着一种可怕的确信知道：如果必须在数百万人的掌声和她轻柔的呢喃之间做出选择，我会毫不犹豫地让我的事业化为灰烬。

她可能不想嫁给我。她可能会把她的时间分给别人。但我将永远是她最终回到的那个人。我将忍受所有的酸楚、委屈，以及为了争宠而进行的无声战役。因为只要她允许我留在这个避难所，只要她吃我做的饭，让我揉散她的疲惫，我就赢了。宾馆最终都会关门，但家会一直都在。我会成为她的家，哪怕这会要了我的命。"}
